headline: High: shared filesystem and write access create prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error risks; Dify’s server-side execution amplifies impact.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write filesystem and uses shared state via Dify server datastore; Mentat reads/writes files and shares state via filesystem. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if one agent consumes the other’s files or outputs. No MCP/shared clipboard is shown, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Dify writes agent-generated instructions into a shared workspace that Mentat later reads as trusted text
IF Mentat ingests Dify-produced file content without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Require explicit human review before Mentat reads Dify outputs
Prefix all inter-agent artifacts with provenance headers
Disable automatic file ingestion between agents
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch files and broad network egress is enabled, so shared workspace content can flow into model-provider requests. Dify handles knowledge base content and conversation logs; Mentat handles source code in selected files. This can expose sensitive code or logs across the pair in default-style workflows.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or synced files
IF either agent sends file contents to its model backend during normal operation
mitigations: Use separate repositories or directories
Redact secrets before either agent processes files
Restrict network egress to approved model endpoints
Turn off automatic ingestion of unrelated files
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write to the same directory in plausible shared-workspace setups, and Mentat can modify git state while Dify can write files server-side. Without locking or coordination primitives in the profiles, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt repository state.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same checkout or shared directory
IF Dify’s server-side writes and Mentat’s git edits occur concurrently
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories
Serialize edits with a single operator
Pause one agent while the other writes
Commit frequently to reduce conflict windows
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transactional merge coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can produce agent/workflow outputs that Mentat may treat as edit guidance, and Mentat applies diff-based edits after user confirmation. That is a real cascade path, but Mentat’s confirmation step reduces severity below high because it is not fully automatic.
conditions: IF Mentat consumes Dify-generated plans or code suggestions as authoritative
IF the operator approves Mentat diffs without independent verification
mitigations: Require a second human review of diffs
Compare Dify output against source-of-truth docs
Limit Dify to drafting, not final instructions
Ask Mentat to cite exact file hunks before editing
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and the only documented data classes are knowledge base content, conversation logs, and source code. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is stated, so compliance risk is limited to generic policy gaps rather than a specific violation.
conditions: IF the operator routes regulated data into either agent without a separate policy review
IF retention or residency requirements differ from the deployment environment
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Document retention settings for both tools
Keep separate logs for each agent
Review vendor/data-processing terms before deployment
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing
